{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that expansive (vs. contractive) nonverbal body postures would increase romantic attraction and the likelihood of receiving positive responses from potential romantic partners, and that this effect would be mediated by perceived dominance and openness.",
  "design": "between-subjects",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Confederate dating application profile photographs featuring either expansive/open or contractive/closed nonverbal body postures",
  "outcome_measure": "Romantic attraction measured by the number of positive match responses ('yes' selections) on an online dating application and trait ratings from online participants",
  "population_and_setting": "Online participants recruited via Amazon Mechanical Turk and users of a GPS-based mobile dating application in the Bay Area, California",
  "sample_size_total": 853,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Online recruitment via Amazon Mechanical Turk and active users of a dating application",
  "analysis_plan": "Independent samples t-tests, chi-square tests of significance, and multilevel mediation models using the Monte Carlo method",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants viewed photograph collages representing target profiles and rated them on dominance and openness."
}
